Quick Answer
iOS 27 focuses on useful refinements, with better Liquid Glass controls, smarter Siri AI, natural-language Shortcuts, Safari web-change alerts, separate alarm volume, improved Photos tools, AirPods EQ, smarter password handling, and several everyday quality-of-life upgrades.
Apple has finally started rolling out iOS 27 to all eligible devices after testing it in beta for months. If you are reading this article, the update is already rolling out. If your iPhone supports it, you can go to Settings, General, Software Update, and update to the latest version.
iOS 27 isn’t a significant jump from what we have seen from iOS 18 to iOS 26. For those who are not aware, Apple has changed the version names to match the year. So instead of iOS 19, they moved it to iOS 26 to match the year 2026.
This year’s iOS 27 is more about refinement and fixing the issues that came along with iOS 26.
One of the biggest updates for most people, at least based on our insight, is the ability to refine the liquid glass design. Apple is now offering a separate setting to make your liquid glass look more frosted or transparent, and also allowing you to set different volumes for the alarms.
Plus, there is a new Siri and plenty of other Siri AI features, such as creating your own shortcuts using natural prompts. Let your password app fix compromised passwords, monitor website changes for free using Safari, and much more.
I have been testing iOS 27 for a few months now, testing its wide variety of features. In this guide, you will learn about the 27 best iOS 27 features that everybody should know and use for a better quality of life.
Table of Contents
Best iOS 27 Features You Should Know and Use
There are tens of new feature additions and improvements in iOS 27. However, not every new feature deserves your attention. There are a few features that really stood out for me and are genuinely useful in day-to-day life that everyone should be aware of. So here are my ten favorite picks before going to the comprehensive list of features.
Adjust Liquid Glass Design Transparency
It is evident that most people hated the new liquid glass design Apple introduced in iOS 26. Apple made the entire UI transparent overnight with a glossy effect, which made text hard to read and was resource-heavy.
Additionally, a few apps failed to adapt to this design perfectly, resulting in a bad user experience. However, Apple didn’t back off from the decision. Since the launch, Apple has continued to refine the liquid glass design to make it better and more usable.
In the latest iOS 27 update, Apple is offering a separate setting that lets you adjust the transparency of the liquid glass design. This setting is different from what we have covered in our TechPP videos, and here is how to use it.
Build Your Own Shortcuts Using Natural Prompts
Extensions and shortcuts are the two easiest ways to add missing features, whether it’s on your iPhone or in any browser. However, creating shortcuts isn’t always an easy task. It involves dealing with plenty of elements and actions, which can be hard for a casual user.
But that’s changing with iOS 27. The new Siri AI will now let you create a new shortcut based on simple, natural prompts. Now you can simply describe a shortcut using natural language, highlighting what it can do. For instance: A shortcut that automatically changes your iPhone wallpaper every morning or a shortcut that reminds you to drink water every two hours.
Since it uses AI behind the scenes, the possibilities are endless. You can describe whatever problem or feature you want to add through the shortcuts, and it will do it for you. However, the current implementation is not reliable for complex extensions. But it is a good start, and it will only get better in future versions.
I found using Claude or Codex to create iPhone shortcuts is the most reliable way, and it works much better for me than using Siri to create shortcuts, which often don’t get the desired results I wanted.
Let Your Password Apps Handle Your Compromised Passwords
When Apple first introduced the Passcodes app in iOS 18, it was super basic and missed a lot of the features found on other passcode management apps at the time. However, Apple continues to add new features, and the recent iOS 27 brings the ability to fix your compromised passwords automatically.
In simple words, if any of your passwords are compromised, your password app will automatically renew them into new passwords without you having to do it manually.
Password management apps are very good at finding your compromised passwords in data breaches. However, previously you had to manually visit every site and change the password yourself. But that’s going to change with iOS 27, where you can simply tap to auto-change the password, and it does it for you.
Monitor Any Web Changes in Real Time
This is my favorite addition to the Safari browser. Probably a feature that can kill many third-party apps. Apple has added a new Notify Me feature to the Safari web browser in iOS 27. It lets Siri AI monitor real-time changes on the website and notify you. Whether it’s an e-commerce price drop, real-time stock changes, or even a new article addition to any webpage, Safari can monitor it for you.
The best part is, you can describe what changes you want to get notified about in a natural prompt, and it does it for you. Also, there are no hard limits on how many trackers or websites you can track, and it lets you track changes every hour. Weekly, monthly, or even daily. The only requirement is that your device should support the Apple Intelligence feature.
Set Separate Volume for Your Alarms
Another feature that Apple should have introduced years ago is the ability to set custom volumes for your alarms in iOS 27. Previously, Apple used to have a single volume for all sounds, including alarms, calls, media, and notifications. In iOS 27, Apple is splitting that up, letting you set separate volume levels for alarms, media, and notifications.
One-Tap Access for Your Wi-Fi and Mobile Data Toggles
If you are someone who frequently adjusts the mobile and Wi-Fi toggles on your iPhone, iOS 27 is getting a very big, useful upgrade. Now, without needing to open the toggle or the entire panel, you can just individually turn your Wi-Fi toggle on and off directly from the toggle. It is enabled by default.
If you have customized it, you can just drag and drop the new network panel to get access to these features.
Auto-Paste Suggestions on Top of Your Keyboard
Another feature that Android users have enjoyed for years is now finally available on iPhone starting with iOS 27. Once you copy text or take a screenshot, the iOS keyboard now automatically suggests the recently copied clipboard text and images, which you can simply tap on and paste wherever you want.
Previously, it required you to long-press, select, and tap on the paste option to do that.
New Custom Equalizer for Your AirPods
Apple is rolling out a custom equalizer in the settings for AirPods. Now, iPhones with iOS 27 have a native AirPods equalizer in Settings to help you customize the audio output.
The new custom equalizer allows you to adjust lows, mids, and high frequencies separately. However, it is only available for devices running on H2 or later Pro devices, and for older devices, users need to rely on Apple’s Adaptive EQ.
Quickly View Photos Captured by You
One of the biggest downsides of iOS Photos is that the images captured from your iPhone are mixed with screenshots, memes, and other downloaded images saved from third-party apps. This makes it extremely hard for you to find the photos captured particularly from your iPhone. In iOS 27, Apple has added a new “Captured by Me” folder to the Photos app. It only shows the photos and videos taken with your iPhone camera, letting you easily find them.
Let Your Earbuds Automatically Pause When They Detect You Have Fallen Asleep
If you use AirPods, Apple has added another useful feature in iOS 27: your AirPods can automatically pause music, podcasts, or whatever you are listening to when they detect that you have fallen asleep.
Most apps these days offer sleep timers that automatically pause after a certain time. However, Apple’s implementation is more dynamic and doesn’t rely on a set time limit. Based on your movement, the AirPods automatically detect when you have fallen asleep and pause the music. This can be extra useful if you are someone like me who falls asleep, and it also eliminates the need for you to set a sleep timer every night.
The Phone App Automatically Shows Relevant Information While You Are on the Call
How many times have you searched for specific information during a call with a service agent? If your answer is often, then Apple has added a very useful feature for you.
With iOS 27, the Phone app on your iPhone now automatically shows relevant information when you are on a call in real time. These include your reservation numbers, order details, confirmation codes, and much more, which Apple can fetch from other Apple services. This eliminates the need for you to search through emails, messages, or other apps while speaking to customer support or during a business call.
Apple’s Mail App Is Now Better at Finding Information
If you use Apple Mail, it is getting a useful update. Starting with iOS 27, Apple says Mail search is upgraded to find more relevant information based on your search.
Now, instead of remembering the exact subject lines, names, or even words in your email, you can just use your natural tone and search for the exact information you want. Apple says the Mail app can now display more relevant information at the top of the search results, and it’s also smarter, as it can automatically identify the query and find the relevant information.
Now, You Can Set an Exact Expiry Time for Your Find My Sharing
If you use Apple’s Find My for location sharing, it is getting a useful update. You can select the exact time when your location sharing should stop. Previously, Apple only allowed you to share your location for an hour, until the end of the day, or until you manually turn it off.
But with iOS 27, Apple is giving you more flexibility, letting you choose a custom time. Now you can set a combination of days along with the hours to share your location. This also eliminates the need for you to manually remember to turn off location sharing if you have set it to indefinitely.
Now, You Can Turn Your Physical Cards Into Digital Passes
Apple Wallet app in iOS 27 lets you convert your physical cards into digital cards and store them in your Apple Wallet. Carrying a physical card can be a hassle, especially if you have multiple cards. It not only makes your wallet bulky, but also makes it hard to find the right one when you need it.
Moreover, there is a high chance that you can forget it, and it could get lost. Now, with the ability to convert your physical cards into digital ones, the Apple Wallet app eliminates all of these pain points. Plus, even if you want to carry a physical card, I would highly suggest converting it into a digital one, which can come in handy sometimes.
Improved AI Writing Tools Across the System
AI writing tools were the first Apple Intelligence features Apple introduced in iOS 18. However, Apple left them out and forgot to update them in iOS 26.
But in iOS 27, with the overall improvements in the AI features and getting close to what it has promised, Apple has also upgraded AI writing tools throughout the system.
Now, these writing tools are more advanced and improved. The best part of these AI writing tools is that they are integrated directly into the workflow.
So if you want to summarize, shorten, or fix spelling mistakes, you don’t need to switch apps. You can generate, rewrite, or correct text directly from your iPhone keyboard. Plus, Apple is also integrating these AI capabilities across the system, including Mail and the Notes app, letting you easily access them anywhere.
Easily Create Calendar Events Without Specific Details
Creating a calendar event requires you to fill in separate details for title, date, time, location, and other details. However, with iOS 27, Apple is making it easy for you to create or edit calendar events.
Now, without needing to fill everything manually, you can just create a calendar event using natural prompts.
For instance, you can ask Calendar to create a birthday event at 4 a.m. tomorrow, and it will do it for you. Calendar app can now understand details such as important keywords, dates (such as tomorrow at 4 PM), a person’s name, and other key details, and automatically create a calendar event. Plus, you can also edit using natural language.
Connect an iPhone Directly to Gym Equipment
If you own an iPhone and want to track your workout data, pairing it with an Apple Watch is the most sensible decision. However, it is expensive and can be overkill for users looking for basic fitness tracking features who don’t need distraction on their wrist.
However, the Apple Watch has this nifty feature where they connect to your gym equipment and receives live workout data, such as your speed, distance, pace, resistance, and the duration of your workout, which you can then measure and analyze in your Apple Health app.
If you do not own an Apple Watch or don’t want to carry it during your workout, Apple in iOS 27 has added the same GymKit functionality directly on your iPhone. So now your iPhone can directly connect to your compatible gym equipment and receive the live workout data. Plus, if you have an Acura Pro 3, you can also connect and track your real-time heart rate information.
Pause Location Sharing Without Disabling It Permanently
If you use Find My to share your location with others, iOS 27 is adding the ability to temporarily hide your location without permanently ending location sharing completely.
In previous versions, if you wanted to temporarily stop sharing your location, whether it’s because your iPhone battery is running out, or if you are planning a surprise, or if you don’t want to reveal your destination, you needed to permanently stop location sharing.
With iOS 27, you can temporarily hide your location from a person. The best part is that the person does not need to be removed, and you also do not need to remember to turn the location back on after the situation has ended.
New Improved Cleanup Tool for Your Photos
I personally hate AI photo editing features inside the Photos app. Recently, both Apple and Google have added several features that are designed to alter and convert your photos into AI-generated ones. However, one feature that I found very useful is the ability to remove unwanted people or objects from a photo directly in the Photos app without relying on third-party tools.
However, Apple’s initial version of the Clean Up Tool isn’t as great as expected. It struggled to remove unwanted distractions from an image. However, with iOS 27, Apple has significantly improved it. Now it’s on par with other clean-up tools that perfectly edit the image naturally, without leaving smudges or empty patches.
Automatically Organize Safari Tabs by Subject
With iOS 27, Apple’s Safari browser can now automatically organize tabs for you. Many other browsers have adopted this feature, but it took some time for Apple to implement it.
If you use the Safari browser and have many tabs open, you can enable the Auto-Organize feature so that it automatically organizes your tabs. This lets you easily find them or close all of them at once.
Generate Your Own Extensions for Safari
Similar to iOS Shortcuts, you can also generate your own extensions using natural prompts in Safari. If you have an Apple Intelligence-supported iPhone, you can just visit the extension tab and give it a natural prompt about what exact features the extension might have, and Apple Intelligence will create a fully working extension for you.
You can just use this extension for an individual web page, or for all the web pages in your Safari browser.
New Siri for Agentic Tasks
Apple is finally close to delivering the Siri it promised two years ago. With iOS 27, Apple is introducing the new Siri, called Siri AI, which is now better at answering your questions and also better at agentic tasks. Plus, it can now search across your Apple apps, including Mail, Messages, Photos, Notes, and all other supported apps, and get information for you.
You can create a reminder, edit a message, organize details, or complete another task. Plus, Siri can also have better context, which means it can remember the information that it gets from other apps. Although at its current stage it is not as advanced as Gemini or other intelligent or agentic AI tools, it is a good start for Apple to deliver what it promised.
It will only get better from now on. Plus, Siri is directly integrated into the system. You can activate it from any screen. Plus, it is free to use without any limitations, except for a few features that Apple might put behind a subscription paywall in the future.
New Wallpaper Extensions
If you customize your iPhone and set a new wallpaper often, this can come in handy. Apple is introducing a new wallpaper extension feature in iOS 27, which expands your wallpaper so it fits correctly based on your iPhone dimensions.
In most cases, if your iPhone wallpaper doesn’t match your iPhone screen dimensions, it can look blurry and pixelated. Plus, if you want to set it as a lock screen wallpaper, it can also affect the depth effect, making the overall wallpaper look blurry and clumsy.
With this new extension wallpaper, Apple now extends the wallpaper to perfectly fit your iPhone’s aspect ratio. The best part is it preserves the main subject and only generates the matching scenery at the image’s edges, so that the subject stays in the middle without being cut off.
Reply Inline to the Messages From Android Users
With the iOS 27 update, Apple is putting an end to another discussion of blue and green bubbles and Apple’s tactics to limit RCS messaging.
Apple iMessage now supports inline replies, where you can directly reply to a specific message sent from your Android friend. This is like a nested reply where you can long-press on any message and tap on Reply. Along with your reply, the other person’s message appears on top, making it easy for them to spot and understand.
New Siri Visual Intelligence
Siri is also now upgraded with better visual intelligence, and it is now live inside your camera app. Now you can spot objects inside your camera and ask Siri to describe them. This can be especially useful for visual intelligence tasks, such as translating the text from a photo, identifying a specific object or food, or extracting the details from a flyer.
Plus, the best part is that, since it is being done by Siri, you can also ask follow-up questions and even delegate tasks, such as adding the extracted information to your calendar or splitting and storing it in any app. Now, adjust your lock screen clock to make it look smaller.
This can be small, but useful for people who often customize their lock screen.
Apple is now letting you adjust the clock size on your iPhone lock screen. Now you can adjust the size of the lock screen clock even smaller. If you feel your clock is covering the important details of your wallpaper, or if you want it to take up less space, you can simply use the smaller clock feature to adjust its size and make it look smaller.
Organize Your Photos Better
While Apple’s Photos app search is smart enough to find the relevant image you are looking for using just natural prompts, Apple is also letting you add individual star ratings and keywords to the photos. Starting with iOS 27, you can rate the photos up to 5 stars and add keywords.
Photos app displays these details while you are browsing your media library, letting these photos stand out from the rest. This makes them easy to spot instead of manually comparing photos to find the best ones from your extensive media library.
Save Photos Directly From Videos
With iOS 27, Apple also introduced the ability to save any frame from a video. You can simply use the Save frame as a photo feature, and the video frame will be saved as a photo. You can save multiple frames as photos.
Here is how:
- Open the Photos app on your Phone
- Play any video and tap on the three-dot menu at the top
- From here, tap on the Save Video frame as a photo option
Get the Most Out of iOS 27
Those are the 27 best iOS 27 features that everyone should know and use.
Apple has officially started rolling out iOS 27. By the time we publish this post, the update is available for all eligible phones. You can update and test out these new features. Detailed videos of how to use the features are coming soon on our TechPP YouTube channel. If you have any issues or if you don’t find this feature on your iPhone, you can comment below. I am happy to help you.

From humble beginnings to the cusp of making history: a look at the rise of the Dockers
It's a Dockers dream 32 years in the making — Fremantle are just one win away from premiership glory.
To their fans, the Dockers are the perpetual underdogs, a team that — according to historian Les Everett — was started to "dilute the West Coast Eagles".
Victorian clubs feared the Eagles were "getting too powerful" following their 1991 grand final appearance and premierships in 1992 and 1994.
There were many names put forward for Western Australia's second team, all with links to the port and sea, including the Pirates, Pelicans, Sharks, Dolphins and even the Doctors after Perth's famous sea breeze, the Fremantle Doctor.
The Dockers joined the competition in 1995, with futuristic purple footy shorts that were the "roomiest shorts in the AFL" compared to the tight fits of the 1980s.
The purple origin
Coach Gerard Neesham paraded the team on the Fremantle Cappuccino Strip, telling reporters at the time "one of our briefs was to be innovative and we have definitely been that."
It was future thinking, with a nod to the past: the purple was inspired by the woollen hats historically worn by port workers, while the red and green colours on the kit came from the maritime signals for port and starboard.
On the docks of Fremantle, wharfies still wear those purple beanies but in 2026, they have club logos.
As for the spirit of Wharfie Time, "it's passion, resilience and having that fight to never give up," said wharfie Jenson Chattaway.
"There will be tears if we win, I'll be crying for sure," added Port Services Officer Mike White.
Frustration forging greats
The early years were tough, with very little in the way of funding. The football club instead relied on 1000 donations of $1,000 each from their original fan group, the Harbour Masters.
But finally purple reigned in 1999. The club won its first game at the hallowed MCG and its first Western Derby, officially stepping out of the Eagles' shadow.
"In round 10, 1999, one of the Victorian newspapers said Melbourne only had to turn up to win the game at the MCG," historian Everett said.
"Fremantle played brilliantly, Tony Modra kicked 10 goals.
"The first derby win the same year was important, after losing the first nine to the Eagles, it was just a great relief really after being trapped as the little sibling to the Eagles."
A year later, in 2000, Matthew Pavalich joined the Dockers. Through his career, he kicked 700 goals and as captain he took the team to its first decider in 2013.
The famous all-rounder played alongside dual Brownlow Medal winner Nathan Fyfe. But it was not to be, and the Hawks shattered the Dockers' premiership dream by 15 points.
Daring to dream again
A new generation of players has taken the Dockers to the decider once again, and for Mr Everett, this is best team Fremantle has ever fielded.
"There is something about the way this team operates, there is a connection that makes it better than any team before," he said.
"It's been organically grown — it doesn't have any father-son gifts in it. Forged through good drafting, good trading, good development.
"That's been the story of Fremantle right from the start, it has been left to its own devices and if it wins the premiership it has done so itself."
Even before the game began, the town was painted purple, and the team immortalised with a massive mural.
But the players will achieve living legend status if they can take home the club's first ever premiership flag.
"If we do win it, I'll be watching the game again, again and again. I'll know every minute of it," Mr Everett said.
"Fremantle supporters, we've put ourselves through some misery, but I have never called myself a long-suffering Fremantle supporter, I have loved it."

It looked like a typical spring evening on Melbourne’s Canning Street when a few dozen picnickers gathered on the grassy median strip on Friday, with drinks in hand.
People in one group who’d come with a full alfresco setting chattered as they ladled punch out of a glass bowl on a wooden table, set with a tablecloth and yellow flowers in a vase. Others sat on picnic blankets, passing around bags of chips.
What set this gathering apart was that it was actually against the rules, given the new ban against drinking on the strip. And the picnic had been organised in protest, part of a political saga that is unfolding on one of inner Melbourne’s most beloved streets.
It began on Monday, when a local bar and bottle shop, the Wine Corner Store, announced on Instagram that, “due to a few unrelenting miserable neighbours who have been non-stop complaining to the council”, consuming alcohol had been outlawed on the median strips on Drummond, Rathdowne and Canning Streets in Carlton North.
The council was reverting to a former classification of the median strips – which are much wider than a typical nature strip – with the effect that they are no longer treated as park spaces. The council said residents had complained about noise, rubbish and unsafe behaviour.
The community fought back to keep a tradition that has endured for many years. While the council ban followed an initial 29-signature petition that a resident submitted in August, a counter petition calling on council to revoke the ban gathered more than 7,707 signatures in just a few days.
The protest drinks on Friday were civilised.
Amid the uproar – and with people loosely uniting under a banner of Free the Strip! – Adam Pulford, the Greens candidate for the seat of Brunswick at the state election, had posted an invitation on social media for people to join him for a peaceful protest.
People milled around, chatting and offering each other drinks and nibbles, talking about the importance of preserving places for building connections outside work and home.
“We need to be building community spaces and not getting rid of them,” said Sam Drummond, who attended the gathering. “Particularly post-Covid, there are very few spaces where people can come together and meet in public, in person.”
Others on the strip on Friday had heeded a call from a Canning Street resident, Rachel Richmond, to gather for the same purpose. As the groups coalesced, Richmond said it was “the most civilised act of civil disobedience I’ve ever participated in”.
“This might seem like a very ridiculously middle class thing to protest,” she said. “I mean, it’s literal champagne socialism but honestly, sitting underneath it is an issue about public space and public enjoyment of space.”
The only disorderly incident the Guardian witnessed on the median strip on Friday was a minor skirmish between a chihuahua and a labrador, both on leads.
However, local councillor Edward Crosling, who represents the Carlton North ward, said there had been “genuine amenity concerns”, especially from people living around the Wine Corner Store, and he believed it was unfair the council had been portrayed in a negative way.
Nevertheless, Crosling said council staff had gone too far in banning drinking outright. “There are some people that have been behaving not fantastically but the majority of people are just having a picnic,” he said.
Crosling said he was working with the council staff to prepare a motion for their next meeting in October, which he anticipated would re-classify the median as open space, and look at “particular” measures to address concerns surrounding the Wine Corner Store.
The venue’s owner, Steve Misfud-Ellul, told Australian Associated Press his business had wrongly copped the blame for large groups choosing to stop on the grass near the wine bar.
“We simply sell retail drinks to people and they choose to stop where they stop,” he said. “Ninety-nine per cent of the time it’s people sitting, picnicking on a patch of grass, with the loudest noise being laughing.”
Misfud-Ellul also stressed the council was not to blame.
“The council actually were fantastic and they acted on every complaint; they came through, they check and they saw there was no problem,” he said.
Despite the councillors pledging to fix the problem, the premier, Ben Carroll, waded in on Friday, sharing a post on social media that said: “Consider this unbanned. Because if council doesn’t reverse it, we will reverse it for them”.
Australian Associated Press contributed to this report

Srinagar, Sep 22: On the occasion of the annual Urs Mubarak of Hazrat Sheikh Syed Abdul Qadir Jilani (RA), Mirwaiz-e-Kashmir Dr. Moulvi Mohammad Umar Farooq delivered a special religious address at the historic Aastan-e-AaliyaDastgeer Sahib (RA), Khanyar, Srinagar.
As per a statement, a large number of devotees attended the spiritually uplifting gathering, including a significant number of women.
In his address, Mirwaiz dwelt upon the fundamental message of Tawheed — the absolute Oneness of Allah Almighty — and highlighted the timeless teachings and spiritual legacy of Hazrat Sheikh Syed Abdul Qadir Jilani (RA).
He said that Hazrat Sheikh Abdul Qadir Jilani (RA) consistently called upon believers to remain firmly attached to the Qur’an and Sunnah, purify their hearts and souls, perform righteous deeds, and place complete trust and reliance in Allah Almighty.
Mirwaiz said that at a time when Muslims across the world are passing through severe challenges, uncertainty and difficult circumstances, the teachings of the revered saint assume even greater relevance. He urged Muslims to strengthen their relationship with Allah Almighty through sincere prayer, genuine repentance, patience, steadfastness, firm faith and unwavering trust in Him.
He emphasised that closeness to Allah must also be reflected in one’s conduct towards fellow human beings, and urged the faithful to imbibe the values of humility, compassion, self-purification, righteous character and service to humanity that formed an integral part of the teachings of Hazrat Sheikh Syed Abdul Qadir Jilani (RA).
Mirwaiz stressed that true spirituality lies in sincere devotion to Allah, adherence to His commandments and following the path shown by the Holy Prophet Muhammad (SAW).
At the conclusion of his sermon and religious discourse, Mirwaiz recited a Manqabat in praise of Hazrat Peeran-e-Peer Sheikh Syed Abdul Qadir Jilani (RA) and paid rich tribute to his enduring religious, spiritual and reformative services to the Muslim Ummah.
Earlier, upon his arrival at Khanyar, Mirwaiz was accorded a warm and enthusiastic welcome by the people.

A British man has died after falling about 61 metres (200ft) while descending from the summit of a mountain in northern Spain, according to local law enforcement.
The 28-year-old mountaineer fell down a vertical gully on the east side of the Torrecerredo – the highest peak of the Cantabrian mountains – on Thursday afternoon, the Spanish Civil Guard for the Asturias region said.
The mountaineer’s remains were located after a rescue team aboard a helicopter flew over the area, the Civil Guard said.
Two specialists were lowered to retrieve the man’s body and his belongings which had been scattered during the fall.
The incident occurred during the descent, about 20 metres below the Torrecerredo peak, the Civil Guard said.
The mountaineer’s body was transported to La Morgal, a regional sports and aviation facility in Llanera near the Asturian city of Gijon.
A spokesperson for the UK Foreign Office said it had contacted local authorities about the death.
Torrecerredo, which has an elevation of about 2,649 metres, is the highest peak of the Picos de Europa mountain range, which is part of the larger Cantabrian Mountains range.

Indian kabaddi teams continued their hunt for a second consecutive gold medal at the Asian Games after both the men’s and women’s sides entered the finals in Aichi-Nagoya on Friday.
While the men’s team thrashed Thailand 66-28, the women’s side beat Nepal 48-24 to book their places in the gold-medal matches.
The prospect of an India-Iran final in both events remains alive, with Iran set to face Chinese Taipei in the other semifinals.
The women’s semifinal began with Pooja, Sanju Devi and Sonali Singhate leading India’s raiding effort against Nepal. However, India’s defence was breached repeatedly, with Ganga Ghimire proving a persistent threat. Ghimire also produced a Super Raid in the first half.
India, though, maintained control and went into the break with a 14-point lead.
Ghimire and Rabina Chaudhary continued to trouble the Indian defence after the interval, but Nepal’s raiders could not match the impact of their Indian counterparts. India inflicted three All Outs during the contest to pull away and secure a comfortable victory.
In the men’s semifinal, the defending champion got off to a flying start, picking up four straight points. Arjun Deshwal, Devank and Ayan shared the raiding duties as India inflicted its first of four All Outs within seven minutes.
Thailand then enjoyed a strong spell in the first half, with Theeradet Chaisit at the heart of its revival. He produced a Super Raid before adding two more points to help Thailand inflict an All Out on India.
But Thailand’s resistance was short-lived. India responded strongly and established a 19-point lead by half-time.
India grew increasingly dominant after the interval as Thailand appeared to tire, allowing the defending champion to cruise into the final.

Call of Duty: Warzone is adding a button to hide all the goofy skins
No more Beavis and Butt-Head in your matches.
For any Call of Duty players who roll their eyes at the growing number of distractingly ridiculous skins, a fix is at hand, at least for one game mode. Season 1 for Modern Warfare 4 will introduce a toggle for Warzone matches that replaces any player skins acquired from other sources around the CoD universe with standard Operator appearances. The toggle is off by default, and it doesn't impact the experience of any other people in a match. Even when the toggle is enabled, the player's own skin will appear as usual, so you can be the lone cartoon character and make everyone else wear camo if you want.
Considering that over the years, the popular FPS has offered players the chance to look like everything from Rambo to Beavis and Butt-Head, matches could look downright ridiculous. Not to mention the added indignity of being offed by a creepy fuzzy creature called Wubz, because that's apparently a thing that you can be. Those players wanting to keep the Warzone experience serious, at least as serious as CoD can ever be, will likely embrace the new option.

Trump's plans for massive arch move ahead
- Published
US President Donald Trump's plans for building a massive arch appear to be moving ahead, after a federal advisory council terminated talks on how to handle the 250-foot structure's possible effects on nearby historic sites.
The council, led by Trump appointees, announced on Thursday it was ending required consultations on the project, saying historic preservation officers from Washington and Virginia had refused to sign off on harm-mitigation plans.
Construction was already expected to begin this month, but opposition has been growing.
On Friday, Democratic Senator Tammy Duckworth blasted plans to use the arch for defence as "foolhardy" and called it "yet another Trump vanity project".
Earlier this week Trump announced that the proposed "Triumphal Arch" would double as a complex to store military equipment, complete with the ability to deploy snipers and drones from the roof and plaza.
In a letter to the Pentagon and Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), Duckworth said they "must reject this foolhardy plan and instead focus on increasing the safety of the airspace".
The arch is to be built just outside Arlington National Cemetery in Virginia, and about 4mi (6km) from Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, the site of the deadly 2025 midair crash between a military helicopter and commercial plane.
"The American people cannot afford to stand witness to Trump's risky plan to place a 250-foot (72m) structure along a busy approach path, especially if he follows through on plans to station snipers on the arch and fly drones," Duckworth wrote in the letter, which was obtained by the BBC's US partner, CBS News.
The FAA, however, ruled last week that the massive structure would not pose a risk to flights coming into and out of the airport.
On Thursday, the Advisory Council on Historic Preservation, led by Trump appointees, announced it was ending required consultations with local officials about how the structure might affect 42 historic properties in the area.
The council said in the announcement that the National Park Service, which oversees federal landmarks, had proposed a plan for mitigating potential harms to those properties, but local historic preservation officers "raised concerns with the purpose and need of the Triumphal Arch". They also questioned whether the service had adequately identified possible harms and planned sufficient actions to address them.
Federal and state officials are not required to reach an agreement on a project's harm-mitigation plans, and those consultations are allowed to be terminated if both sides can't agree. The council expects to submit a final report on the process early next month.
Meanwhile, Democratic Virginia Congressman Don Beyer says excavation work on the site where the arch will stand has already begun.
Beyer, who is leading congressional opposition to the arch, said he found workers operating heavy equipment when he visited the site on Thursday who told him they were "conducting archaeological work to evaluate the composition of the soil".
That is "deeply troubling", Beyer said, particularly because the administration is required to give 48 hours notice before work can begin.
"The Administration appears to be pushing ahead with activity at the site even while it still has not done the basic work necessary to understand the consequences of this project," Beyer wrote.
A rendering of the design from earlier this year includes a golden, winged Lady Liberty on the top of the arch, flanked by two gold eagles, and with the phrases "One Nation Under God" and "Liberty and Justice for All" inscribed in gold on either side of the structure.

Saudi Arabia says it intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis, with the latest attacks pushing oil prices to a one-week high over fears of spiralling supply disruptions.
The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said the missiles were aimed at Taif in western Saudi Arabia and the Yanbu area on the Red Sea, with the Houthis claiming their attacks were aimed at “a sensitive target” in the capital Riyadh and on Saudi Aramco facilities in Yanbu.
Oil prices climbed about 3%, but trade was volatile and prices came off session highs after reports the US and Iran discussed reopening the strait of Hormuz.
The escalating attacks threaten Saudi Arabia’s ability to export oil through the Red Sea at a time when the strait of Hormuz is disrupted and the kingdom’s east-west pipeline is only now resuming operations after drone strikes earlier this month. The Houthis declared a naval blockade on the kingdom in July, opening a second theatre in the US-Iran war.
It was not clear whether there was any damage or casualties in either Taif or Yanbu, the main alternative route for Saudi oil.
The Houthis seized the whole Yemeni western coast in a lightning offensive nearly two weeks ago that brought them to the shores of the Red Sea’s strategic Bab el-Mandeb waterway.
Yemen’s internationally recognised government pressed world leaders on Thursday for help defeating the militants, saying that their new perch along one of the world’s busiest waterways presents an international economic risk.
While claiming that their blockade only applies to Saudi shipping and there remains no threat to commercial shipping on the Red Sea, the Houths have also warned other nations not to get involved.
But the vice-president of the internationally recognised government council urged world leaders at the UN general assembly not to trust the Houthis’ assurances – and to see a bigger picture in the crisis around the strait.
“The Houthi militias’ use of the safety of navigation as a tool for blackmail threatens not only Yemen. It is taking hostage the entire global economy,” said vice-president, Abdullah Abdulkader al Alimi-Bawzer.
Arguing that protecting the strait “is the responsibility of every economy that depends on secure supply chains, energy security and freedom of navigation,” he urged the international community to keep weapons and technology from getting into the rebels’ hands.
The Saudi-backed government’s forces had earlier repelled overnight attacks by the Houthis on a key supply route to Yemen’s third-biggest city Taiz from the southern port city of Aden where the internationally recognised administration is based, government sources said.
The Houthis have kept up pressure along a steep, winding mountain pass known as Hejat al-Abd, a lifeline for government forces and the only route for goods and residents to reach Taiz and travel abroad. Seizing parts of the road could allow the Houthis to tighten their grip around the city and deal another blow to the government, which has struggled to regain the initiative since losing the western coast.
Riyadh’s foreign ministry said on Friday that Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan would hold an urgent meeting of their chiefs of staff to discuss ways to support repel the Houthi attacks under their joint defence agreement. Under the defence pact, all three countries agreed that an armed attack on any one of them would be treated as an attack on all three.
Officials in Pakistan are said to be deeply worried about being dragged into the never-ending war unfolding across the Middle East.
With Reuters and the Associated Press

Q: I get headaches whenever I use my phone or computer for a long time. Are screens damaging my brain?
A: Screens are not known to damage the brain simply through use, but prolonged use can cause eye strain, dry eyes, blurred vision, neck and shoulder tension and headaches. Poor posture, glare and inadequate breaks can worsen symptoms. Follow the 20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes, look about 20 feet away for 20 seconds. Adjust brightness, reduce glare and blink regularly. Frequent or severe headaches, especially without screen use, need medical evaluation.
Q: Is every headache a migraine?
A: No. Headaches can result from stress, tension, dehydration, poor sleep, eye strain, infections, sinus problems, stomach problems or migraine. Migraine may cause throbbing pain, nausea and sensitivity to light or sound, though symptoms vary. A new, unusually severe or rapidly worsening headache, especially with weakness, confusion, fainting, seizures, vision changes, fever or difficulty speaking, needs urgent medical attention.
Q: I have a headache, so I take a painkiller immediately. Is that okay?
A: Occasional appropriate use may be fine for some people, but frequent painkiller use can cause medication-overuse headaches and, depending on the medicine, stomach, kidney or liver problems. If you regularly need painkillers for headaches, find the cause rather than repeatedly treating the symptom.
Q: Do I really need a flu shot if I usually get only a mild flu?
A: Influenza can be mild but can also cause serious illness, especially in high-risk people. Flu vaccination reduces the risk of influenza and its complications, though it does not prevent every cold or respiratory virus. Because influenza viruses change, seasonal vaccination is recommended for many people according to individual risk. Ask your doctor if it is appropriate for you, particularly if you have chronic diseases, are pregnant or belong to another recommended group.
Q: Can the flu shot give me influenza?
A: No. Injectable flu vaccines do not contain live influenza virus capable of causing influenza. Soreness, tiredness or a mild fever can occur briefly after vaccination and usually reflect an immune response. You can also catch another respiratory virus around the same time. Remember that protection takes time to develop.
Q: My eyes burn after looking at my phone for hours. Do I need “screen glasses”?
A: Not necessarily. Digital eye strain can cause burning, dryness, temporary blurred vision and headaches because we blink less while concentrating. Take regular breaks, blink consciously, reduce glare and keep the screen at a comfortable distance. Prescription glasses may help if you have an underlying vision problem. Blue-light glasses are not a magic solution. Persistent pain or significant vision changes need an eye examination.
Q: Does using a phone in the dark permanently damage eyesight?
A: Ordinary phone use in a dark room has not been shown to permanently damage eyesight, although the bright screen against a dark background can cause strain, dryness or headaches. Keep some ambient light on and adjust screen brightness. Persistent blurred or double vision, eye pain or headaches should not simply be blamed on the phone.
Q: I use my phone until I fall asleep. Does it really affect sleep?
A: It does. Screen use keeps the brain engaged, while light from screens can affect the body’s sleep-wake rhythm. Messages, videos and social media can be particularly stimulating. Keep the phone away from the bed, choose quieter activities before sleep and maintain a regular bedtime. Persistent sleep problems need further evaluation.
Q: Can sitting in front of a screen all day cause neck and back pain?
A: Yes. Prolonged sitting and poor posture can cause neck, shoulder and back pain, while looking down at a phone can add neck strain. Change position regularly, keep the screen at a comfortable height, support your back and move around during the day. Exercise and strengthening can help. Persistent pain, numbness, weakness or pain spreading into an arm or leg should be assessed.
Q: I feel dizzy and get a headache after spending hours on my phone. Is it because of radiation?
A: There is no good evidence that ordinary mobile-phone use causes headaches or dizziness through the radiation emitted by phones. However, prolonged use can indirectly contribute through eye strain, poor posture, dehydration, lack of sleep and inactivity. Look at the whole pattern and take regular breaks. If headaches or dizziness keep returning, particularly without screen use, consult your doctor.
Q: Are “sugar-free” foods healthy?
A: No. “Sugar-free” does not mean nutritious. Sugar-free biscuits, chocolates and snacks may still be high in calories, refined flour, saturated fat or salt. Some contain sugar alcohols or other sweeteners that can cause gas, bloating or diarrhoea when consumed in excess. They may also keep our preference for very sweet foods alive. Sugar-free is a label, not a health certificate. Always check the complete nutrition label.
Q: Are zero-sugar drinks harmless?
A: Not necessarily. They can be a better choice than sugary drinks if you are trying to reduce sugar and calories, but they are not automatically healthy. Some sweeteners can cause gas, bloating, abdominal cramps or diarrhoea, particularly in people with sensitive digestion or IBS. If a particular drink repeatedly causes bowel discomfort, stop it and see whether symptoms improve. Zero sugar does not mean zero consequences.
Public Advisory: Not every health problem needs a tablet—and not every health myth deserves to be believed. From WhatsApp remedies and “natural” cures to advice from friends and relatives, health information can easily become distorted. Before starting, stopping or changing a treatment, ask the doctor—not the WhatsApp group.
NOTE: These responses are for general awareness and do not replace professional medical advice. Older adults often have multiple illnesses and medicines, so individual medical advice should be taken from a qualified healthcare professional.

It was at the 1992 Olympics in Barcelona when the mutterings about a new "secret weapon" started.
Dozens of Great Britain athletes had been taking a new product that increased muscle mass and improved athletic performance – a "wonder pill" that didn't fall foul of any doping rules.
They were talking about creatine.
Now found in tubs and bags on many supermarket shelves and tagged in your social feeds, it is the supplement of choice for millions of people and one of the most scientifically researched.
But back then, when it came on the scene at the very top of British elite sport, there were suspicions and stigma around the use of any substance described as 'performance enhancing' – even if it was legal.
From the minute an athlete wakes, to the moment they go to bed, they are thinking about how they can optimise their performance and recovery.
Today, creatine is just one of a long list of supplements taken by elite athletes in this pursuit of marginal gains. Some help with muscle size and strength, while others correct deficiencies in the diet.
"There are various reports in the literature of some studies that say maybe up to 90% of athletes take supplements. I often jokingly say that means 10% are lying," says Prof Graeme Close, professor of human physiology at Liverpool John Moores University.
"The sports teams that I've worked in, I think that's probably closer to 100% of athletes will be taking some form of supplementation."
So, what do supplements actually do and why do athletes take them? And in the world of strict liability, where elite athletes are solely responsible for what they put in their bodies, how do they make sure they stay clean?
While experts like Close advocate for seeking to meet nutritional needs through food in the first instance, it may not always be possible or practical to do this - and that is where supplements come in.
Take, for example, creatine, which is found naturally in meat and fish.
"You would need the best part of a kilogram of raw chicken a day to get the amount of creatine you need," says Close. But it is unsafe to eat raw poultry because of the food poisoning risk from harmful bacteria.
Creatine is a natural compound in the body produced in the kidneys, liver and pancreas. It is a quick source of energy for muscles, which is especially important for short-duration, high intensity activities such as sprinting.
Its big break as a supplement came in the 1990s when two scientists who had been researching it for two decades shared their findings with Steve Jennings, whose Maxim sports nutrition company supplied products to the British Olympic team.
During the 1992 Barcelona Games, investigative reporter Doug Gillon had learned of a 'secret trial' involving British athletes and seen a box of their Ergomax C150 – effervescent creatine tablets. He wrote that if the scientists' claims - that creatine could improve explosive athletic performance by 1-3% - were true, then "sport may never be the same again".
In terms of sport supplements and nutrition, he was right. By the time of the next Olympics in 1996, an estimated 80% of athletes were taking creatine, and since then it has become mainstream, with research suggesting there may be cognitive benefits as well as physical.
According to the Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition, the creatine breakthrough of the 1990s had "launched a new era in sports nutrition" and "sparked exploration into other supplements".
The global dietary supplements market size was valued at $209.5bn (£154bn) in 2025 and is projected to grow to $431.7bn (£317.4bn) by 2033, according to Grand View Research., external
Close, who oversaw nutrition for last year's British and Irish Lions rugby union tour, sees supplements as the "final piece of the jigsaw" rather than a starting point.
"What we're talking about is small margins of benefit, where actually these athletes who focus on the food, I think what you often find is that they've got the big-ticket items right," he says.
"So they're seeing great performance benefits because their overall diet is immaculate.
"They might be missing out on the one per-centers, but they've really nailed the 99 per-centers. And they often do better than those who chase the one per-centers but have not given enough attention to the 99 per-centers."
Australian cyclist Nicole Frain agrees, adding: "I'm a pretty big believer that they are called sport supplements. They are there to supplement the things you already do right.
"I don't think supplements are the answer to fix my problems.
"You need to be eating a balanced diet, training well, sleeping right, recovering well, hydrating – all of those things – before we add in all of the extras."
Close puts protein powders top of the list of supplements taken by athletes he works with, followed by creatine and vitamin D.
Protein powders maximise muscle repair and contribute to muscle growth, while creatine is a quick source of energy for muscles and important in short-duration, high-intensity activities like sprinting. Vitamin D, meanwhile, is essential for bone health and supports muscle function.
Other popular supplements include carbohydrate gels, which Close says were key in the first sub-two hour marathon run earlier this year by Kenyan long-distance runner Sabastian Sawe.
"As sport nutritionists we were all fascinated at what the fuelling programme was, and it was the sports drinks and gels that played a huge part of that fuelling," Close says.
"There was a calculation done of what it would take to break the two-hour marathon, and that did involve making sure that over 100 grams of supplemental carbohydrate were ingested per hour.
"And the reports coming out of the recent sub-two-hour marathon was that it was 110 grams of carbohydrate per hour that was achieved."
Supplements can improve performance, but there is an uneasy ring to describing them as 'performance enhancing' because of the association with banned substances and anti-doping rule violations.
So what determines whether something is on the World Anti-Doping Agency's (Wada) banned list?
"For Wada to put anything on the list, it's got to hit two out of three criteria: dangerous to health, performance enhancing, and against the spirit of sport," Close explains.
"So just because something enhances performance, if it's not dangerous to health and not against the spirit of sport, Wada will not touch it.
"So creatine is a good example.
"Though something like an anabolic steroid, where it's against the spirit of sport to be injecting yourself for a performance benefit, it's dangerous to health and it's performance enhancing - that hits all three."
But taking a supplement still carries anti-doping risks.
"No guarantee can be given that any particular supplement is free from prohibited substances," UK Anti-Doping advice states, urging athletes to "be vigilant" in using them.
And if you test positive for a prohibited substance, consuming it unintentionally can result in the same four-year ban as if you deliberately took it.
There are supplement-testing programmes which batch test products before they are sold to make sure they do not contain any Wada-prohibited substances.
One of those is Informed Sport, which says as many as one in 10 supplements is contaminated with ingredients and compounds prohibited in sport and points to a study carried out by the Anti-Doping Knowledge Centre that showed product contamination was responsible for 8% of all anti-doping violations between 2005 and 2022.
While Informed Sport is a very well used system among athletes, Wada makes it clear that quality assurance schemes can reduce but do not eliminate the risk of an anti-doping infringement.
If you do accept the risk, you need to be organised to keep track.
In the case of Great Britain rower Heidi Long, it takes a spreadsheet.
"I've recorded the batch number of every product that I've taken and its expiry date because if you take it after the expiry date the Informed Sport [certification] is no longer viable," she says.
Close says he has also done site visits to factories to see where the supplements are made to check the manufacturing processes because "the risk of failing a drugs test is huge".
There are risks to the general population too, he adds, saying: "You can be buying supplements off the internet that are made in somebody's garage and you've got no idea of the manufacturing processes."
He points to studies on creatine products which have found there is no creatine in them and so "you're completely wasting your money" and that in the worst case scenario it may contain substances that are dangerous to your health.
"So it is really important that the message is that while they can play a small role, the safety considerations are the key factor," he says.
There is, however, more than one way for an elite athlete to chase a competitive edge – and some are going back to basics.
For every trending supplement, there is an unprocessed, wholefood alternative – from the anti-inflammatory benefits of turmeric, staving off cramp with pickle juice or consumption of high-nitrate foods like beetroot before competition.
It is what Close calls a "food-first" or "food-only" approach and something he says every athlete should use as a starting point.
The latest to have its moment in the spotlight is an ancient Ethiopian grain called teff.
Used for thousands of years in traditional east African diets, teff is now making its mark globally in performance nutrition.
In comparison to other popular grains like wheat, rice and quinoa, teff has a high mineral content and is rich in calcium, iron and vitamin C. Naturally gluten-free and good for the gut, it is also unique for being a 'complete' protein, meaning it provides all nine essential amino acids required for human nutrition.
These superfood credentials have caught the attention of some of the world's best athletes over the years, from Olympic champion marathon runner Haile Gebrselassie to seven-time Grand Slam singles champion Venus Williams, and it is now becoming a more common sight on UK supermarket shelves.
British boxer Fran Hennessy was introduced to teff by her nutritionist and it is now part of her daily routine.
"I've never looked back," she says. "What I'm putting in my body is good fuel and energy and teff has so much. It energises you so much before a workout and it gives you the fibre you need."
As well as boosting her performances, Hennessy credits teff with being key to recovery.
She says: "Each meal I'm having there's a reason behind and everything that's in it there's a reason behind... I know what I'm putting in my body is fuelling me, recovering me, energising me."
Cost is another consideration when athletes are deciding on supplements.
"The supplement industry is really expensive," says Long. "And we're definitely not made of money. So I think it's really picking and choosing when you want to put that investment in."
She says it makes sense to have more supplements around racing time "when the performance is super critical and very time dependent".
"[But] on a daily basis if I can get the protein intake from my dinner and a glass of milk or yoghurt and breakfast then actually I was going to be eating that food anyway so it's not as expensive."
And then there is taste.
"I would much rather enjoy a coffee in the morning with friends or while I'm working rather than have one of the gels," she says. "Some of the gels ... you'll end up holding your nose when you take it.
"I guess it's just like the enjoyment of what you're taking, you know, it's nicer to eat food than it is to take supplements."

Bushra Bano cleared the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission examination in 2017 with Rank 6, becoming a PCS Officer and later a sub-divisional magistrate. She studied on her own, without coaching, while working full-time and raising two children with her engineer husband. She sat for the UPSC exam twice — in 2019 and 2021 — before securing Rank 234 and clearing the Indian Police Service.
On September 14, 2026, she was transferred from her post as additional SP of Kharagpur in West Bengal’s Paschim Medinipur district, a day after propaganda news channels and Right-wing accounts targeted her for using the Arabic words, ‘Assalamu Alaikum’, ‘Jazakallah’, and ‘Inshallah’, in a video.
In the clip, Bushara is heard commending a government-aided residential coaching academy for minorities, women and SC/ST students at Aligarh Muslim University. While she spoke, she said the three phrases in Arabic. She said, “Assalamu Alaikum. My name is Bushra Bano… ” at first. Towards the end, she said, “…If they (the students) stay and study through the RCA then Inshallah many more people will move forward like me and get the opportunity to serve their country.” At the end she ended her video by saying, “Thank you, Jazakallah”.
“Assalamu Alaikum” is a common greeting which means “Peace be upon you”; “Inshallah” translates to “God willing”, and the phrase “Jazakallah” means “May God Reward You”. The reader might note that these are not religious phrases but greetings and wishes.
A simple video, made by a Muslim IPS officer who used a few Arabic phrases, sent ripples across the Right-wing ecosystem. On September 13, propaganda outlet Sudarshan News, which has its own national TV channel, shared the video on X and said, “Starting with ‘Assalamualaikum,’ slipping in ‘Inshallah’ midway, and wrapping up with ‘Jazakallah’, Bushra Bano… shared how she came from Saudi Arabia and became an IPS officer in India… She made full use of the scheme being run by the government at Aligarh Muslim University.”
“अस्सलाम वाले कुम” से शुरू कर बीच में “इंशाल्लाह” कहते हुए “जज़ाकल्लाह” पर किया खत्म,
खड़गपुर में एडिशनल एसपी के तौर पर तैनात बुशरा बानो ने बताया कि सऊदी अरब से आ कर वो कैसे भारत में बनीं IPS..
सरकार द्वारा अलीगढ़ मुस्लिम यूनिवर्सिटी में चलाई जा रही स्कीम का उठाया भरपूर फायदा.… pic.twitter.com/foYKjihMV2
— Sudarshan News (@SudarshanNewsTV) September 13, 2026
Soon, a barrage of online trolls started targeting Bano. An X handle called @HinduLegalFund posted on X that a complaint had been filed with the West Bengal home secretary regarding the video. “She began with Assalamualaikum, used Inshallah, ended with Jazakallah — and did not use Vande Mataram or Jai Hind…” the post read. Additionally, it stated that a serving officer should maintain “neutrality and national expressions in public communication”.
Complaint filed with West Bengal Home Secretary regarding IPS Bushra Bano’s official video statement.
She began with Assalamualaikum, used Inshallah, ended with Jazakallah — and did not use Vande Mataram or Jai Hind.
A serving officer representing the Indian state should…
— Hindu Legal Fund (@HinduLegalFund) September 13, 2026
Several Right-wing accounts, including @JaipurDialogues and @MeghUpdates, also shared the video and complained that no ‘Vande Mataram’ or ‘Jai Hind’ had been used by the IPS officer.
A notification issued by the government of West Bengal on Monday stated that Bano, alongside two other WBPS officers, was being transferred to a different posting “in public interest”. She has been made the deputy commandant of the state armed police 4th battalion. The notification does not state any reason behind the transfer.
West Bengal Government reshuffles 3 police officers with immediate effect; Partha Ghosh appointed as Addl SP, Kharagpur, Paschim Medinipur.
Subhendu Mandal posted as Addl DC, Chandannagar
Dr. Bushara Bano, transferred as Dy. CO, SAP 4th Bn. pic.twitter.com/MHu5WK4De1
— ANI (@ANI) September 14, 2026
It should be common knowledge that Arabic is a language and Islam is a religion. Muslims use Arabic extensively for religious purposes, but Arabic is not synonymous with Islam. In other words, none of these expressions is simply a ‘Muslim word’ in the narrow linguistic sense. They are Arabic phrases whose meanings and histories intersect with Islamic religious usage, but they are not exclusive to Islam. The tradition of greeting a person with ‘Peace be upon you’, for example, exists in other languages and religious traditions — the Hebrew expression ‘shalom aleichem’, for example, literally means ‘peace be upon you’ and is common in Jewish religious literature. None of this, however, came in the way of pro-BJP handles slamming the officer for her alleged religion posturing.
Sudarshan News editor Suresh Chavhanke, whose history of peddling misinformation and communal propaganda is well documented, called Bano’s case ‘UPSC Jihad’.
Even if one were to accept this as an instance of religious posturing, it would hardly be the first time a police officer has done so. What stands out, however, is how differently such conduct is received depending on the community to which the officer belongs.
In May 2026, IPS officer C V Anand invited priests to perform a puja in his office on the day he took charge as director general of police of Telangana.
Senior IPS officer CV Anand taking charge as Telangana DGP. pic.twitter.com/5ZSSAT6K3w
— Piyush Rai (@Benarasiyaa) May 2, 2026
He himself posted about this on X. No one batted an eyelid. Anand is still serving as the DGP of Telangana.
Anand wrote, “As per the muhurtham , I reached the DGP office at Lakdikapul with my family , took the salute and followed the pujari into the dgp chambers where the puja and blessings were done.”
It was a very busy and perhaps the biggest day for me and my family . As per the muhurtham , I reached the DGP office at Lakdikapul with my family , took the salute and followed the pujari into the dgp chambers where the puja and blessings were done.
Then at 11:05 AM , signed… pic.twitter.com/wlkJX8hszp
— CV Anand IPS (@CVAnandIPS) May 1, 2026
More such instances are not difficult to find.
In Uttar Pradesh’s Sambhal, a circle officer named Anuj Chaudhary, who was an accused of firing during the violence at the Shahi Jama Masjid in November 2024, was pictured joining a Hindu religious procession in January 2025. He was accused of participating in religious rituals while on duty and violating service conduct rules. A complaint was filed by retired IPS officer and Azad Adhikar Sena president Amitabh Thakur, following which a probe was launched.
The same year, on Holi, Chaudhary had stated: “Holi comes once a year, Jumma comes 52 times. If you want to serve sevai, you must also eat gujiya.” Again, an investigation was initiated, and Chaudhary was eventually given a clean chit.
In May 2025, he was transferred from Sambhal to Chandausi, some 30 km away. Three months later, in August, Chaudhary was promoted to the role of additional superintendent of police (ASP). His colleagues and senior officers, including SP K K Bishnoi and ASP Rajesh Kumar Srivastava, marked the occasion with a felicitation ceremony.
Was there no outrage when Anuj Chaudhary carried a mace and marched in a religious procession in uniform? There was, from one section, but he went on to be promoted. Bano’s case panned out differently. The principle, presumably, is that the same rules apply to everyone. In practice, however, some seem to be considerably more equal than others. And if Bushra Bano’s transfer was, as the government put it, “in public interest”, one is left wondering exactly which ‘public’ that interest was meant to serve.
Bano’s transfer set off a series of critical reactions from the Opposition. Several politicians alleged that the transfer was a direct fallout of her use of Arabic phrases. Comparing the incident with Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s inauguration of the Parliament “with sengol & bare chested sadhus”, Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra remarked, “…We are a nation gone mad, poisoned with hate & bigotry. God Save India”.
For a country whose Prime Minister inaugurated new Parliament with sengol & bare chested sadhus, transferring a Muslim IPS officer for saying Assalamalaikum & Inshallah is ridiculous. We are a nation gone mad, poisoned with hate & bigotry. God Save India.
— Mahua Moitra (@MahuaMoitra) September 15, 2026
Former Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Mehbooba Mufti also criticised the move, saying the transfer, which was followed by the West Bengal CM “calling an election a ‘test’ of Muslim loyalty”, was “a veiled threat to the community”. “…First our food, clothes and marriages , now even our vocabulary and our votes are being policed”, she added.
Congress MP Imran Pratapgarhi took to X to condemn the move. “A hate-mongering TV channel first sensationalized that video by posting it and incited online trolling against the female IPS officer, and instead of standing by her, the state government transferred her the very next day. What kind of India are you building, @narendramodi ji? @IPS_Association, are you watching this?”, he wrote.

Weeks after US President Donald Trump asked artificial intelligence (AI) companies in the US not to slow down the development of the technology in an attempt to maintain dominance over China, Washington and Beijing on Friday (local time) decided to set up a "communication channel" for AI-related incidents. The announcement was made by the White House following a short summit on breakthroughs, AFP reported. The announcement came days after Chinese President Xi Jinping visited the US President in Washington, where the two leaders held discussions on several matters, including AI, bilateral trade and the ongoing war in Iran. The White House, in a fact sheet, said that the US and China established a "US-China Super Intelligence (SI) Dialogue to exchange views on risks and benefits" of the technology, adding that the two leaders had agreed to use the term SI rather than AI. The next exchange is likely to occur in November, the fact sheet added. Before the summit, the US President said, "Super Intelligence (SI) will be a big topic of discussion, but I want to leave it exactly where it is." In a Truth Social post, he added, "That is China's position also." While Trump has consistently dismissed fears that rapidly evolving technology could pose a threat to humanity, despite two of the leading AI companies in the world issuing a warning, his Chinese counterpart took a more measured approach and expressed support for the idea that the technology should be developed under human control. Xi also called for the two sides to manage their superpower rivalry and ensure that AI development continues to remain under human control. He added, "We have both the capability and responsibility to develop and manage AI for good and ensure that the development of AI is always under human control." Separately, Trump and Xi also confirmed that they would meet for a third and fourth time this year at two international summits that will be held in China and the US. The White House also highlighted several agreements reached during the visit, including China's commitment to purchase at least 10 million metric tons of US coal in 2027 and 2028. The two countries also agreed to provide more favourable tariff terms for $30 billion worth of "non-sensitive goods" traded in each direction. In addition, two Chinese pandas were set to arrive at a US zoo. Throughout Xi's visit, Trump rolled out the red carpet for him, treating the Chinese President to a state banquet attended by tech titans, military parades, a flyover, and a tour of his new White House helipad and ballroom. The latest developments highlight the growing importance of AI in US-China relations, with both countries seeking to address the opportunities and risks associated with the rapid advancement of the technology. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued red alerts for five districts, orange alerts for five districts and yellow alerts for three districts for September 26. On September 27, red alerts have been issued for four districts, orange alerts for four districts and yellow alerts for five districts. CM Pushkar Singh Dhami asked officials to remain especially vigilant in districts placed under red and orange alerts, keep a constant watch on vulnerable locations and ensure relief and rescue arrangements are ready beforehand to respond swiftly to any emergency. He also ordered district emergency operation centres to remain operational and directed authorities to promptly relay weather warnings to the ground level. The weather department has predicted heavy to very heavy rainfall in several areas, with extremely heavy showers likely at isolated locations. Authorities have been advised to remain on high alert due to the risk of landslides and road disruptions in hilly regions, rising water levels in rivers and streams, and waterlogging across the plains, according to ANI. For September 26, Saturday, the IMD has placed Bageshwar, Pithoragarh, Champawat, Nainital and Udham Singh Nagar under a red alert. Dehradun, Pauri Garhwal, Rudraprayag, Chamoli and Almora have been issued orange alerts, while Haridwar, Uttarkashi and Tehri Garhwal are under yellow alerts. On September 27, Sunday, Dehradun, Tehri Garhwal, Pauri Garhwal and Haridwar are forecast to remain under red alert. Orange alerts have been issued for Uttarkashi, Chamoli, Nainital and Rudraprayag, while Bageshwar, Almora, Champawat, Udham Singh Nagar and Pithoragarh are under yellow alert. On September 28, Monday, Nainital, Dehradun, Tehri, Uttarkashi, Chamoli, Rudraprayag, Haridwar and Pauri Garhwal may witness thunderstorms with lightning, gusty winds of 30-40 kmph and intense to extremely heavy spells of rain at some locations. Other parts of Uttarakhand could also see isolated thunderstorms, lightning, squalls reaching 30-40 kmph and heavy to very heavy rainfall. Meanwhile, areas located at elevations of 4,000 metres and above may also experience snowfall from September 25 to 28, as per a report by Hindustan Times. Dhami said officials had been instructed to maintain special vigilance along the Char Dham Yatra route in view of the weather forecast and warnings issued by the Meteorological Department, and to ensure that all necessary arrangements were in place. “In view of the forecast and warning issued by the Meteorological Department, instructions have been given to officials to exercise special vigilance regarding the Char Dham Yatra and ensure necessary arrangements,” Dhami said. He added, "The safety of local residents as well as all tourists and pilgrims coming here is our topmost priority. We appeal to everyone to exercise caution keeping in view the weather conditions, avoid unnecessary travel, and follow the guidelines issued by the administration. “Keeping in view the weather, instructions have been given to @uksdrf , @NDRFHQ and other rescue teams to remain on alert mode,” the CM concluded. Disaster Management and Rehabilitation Minister Madan Kaushik also spoke with Secretary Vinod Kumar Suman to review the weather conditions and the state’s preparedness. He asked officials to closely track the situation and remain ready to respond to any emergency. Following the Chief Minister’s directions, Suman held a meeting with representatives from all 13 districts on Friday and asked them to remain on high alert. He directed district administrations to keep a close watch on vulnerable locations, ensure that emergency operation centres remain functional and promptly communicate every weather warning to the ground level. Officials have also been told to monitor water levels in rivers, streams, gad-gaderas and other water bodies continuously. Arrangements should be made to move residents in nearby areas to safer locations if water levels begin to rise. JCBs and other essential machinery are to be reportedly positioned at strategic points along landslide-prone roads and locations to ensure blocked routes can be reopened quickly. District emergency operation centres have been instructed to function round the clock, with regular coordination among police, SDRF, fire services, health, Public Works, drinking water, power and other departments. Relief and rescue personnel, along with the required equipment and resources, should be deployed in vulnerable areas whenever necessary. Suman also directed authorities to regulate traffic on mountain roads according to weather and road conditions and discourage unnecessary travel through areas prone to landslides and heavy rainfall. Residents living near rivers, streams and seasonal water channels should be issued regular warnings and advised against approaching riverbanks or entering fast-moving waters, the statement said. Authorities have been asked to maintain special surveillance along Char Dham routes, major tourist spots and other vulnerable locations to safeguard pilgrims and tourists. All necessary arrangements should be made in advance so that rescue and relief operations can be launched with minimal delay during an emergency, it noted. Suman urged district administrations to maintain heightened vigilance and ensure there is no lapse in preparedness amid the prevailing weather conditions. He also appealed to residents to follow advisories issued by the weather department and district administrations, avoid non-essential travel and keep away from rivers, streams and landslide-prone areas. No, Netanyahu wasn’t arrested during his UN visit, but those protesting against him were
Dozens of people were arrested in New York City while protesting against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's participation in the United Nations General Assembly on Thursday.
Thousands of people took part in protests held across the city, including a march organised by Jewish Voice for Peace and the Palestinian Youth Movement outside the UN headquarters.
Actors Susan Sarandon and Hannah Einbinder, as well as activist and whistleblower Chelsea Manning, were among the protesters arrested during a sit-in that blocked a main road leading to the UN.
Handcuffed and escorted by a New York Police Department (NYPD) officer, Einbinder was recorded in a video shared on social media saying, “Netanyahu out of New York, no bombs on Lebanon, no bombs on Iran, stop the genocide.”
Police also arrested politicians and political candidates, including New York City Council members Alexa Avilés, Linda Sarsour, Jennifer Gutiérrez, Chi Ossé, Darializa Avila-Chevalier, and Aber Kawas.
